newsitem.title: ROMANIA: AIRTOUCH, FRANCE TELECOM WIN ROMANIA GSM TENDER.
newsitem.headline: AIRTOUCH, FRANCE TELECOM WIN ROMANIA GSM TENDER.

text.p: AirTouch Communications Inc of U.S. and France Telecom have won a tender for two licences to install and operate a GSM digital cellular phone network in Romania, the Communications Ministry said.

A ministry commission has declared the two telecomm groups as winners after studying offers submitted by six consortia which entered the competition this year, the ministry said in a statement on Friday.
The ministry expects the licences to become operational by early next month, the ministry statement said.

The tender requires the companies to cover within the next 18 months of winning the tender the main cities of Bucharest, Bacau, Brasov, Cluj, Constanta, Craiova, Galati and Timisoara, as well as GSM coverage along European transit routes in Romania within the main roads crossing the country.
The licence has a ten-year validity and frequency concession tax amounts to $50 million per licence.
Initial number of chennels allocated per operator amounted to 22, the statement also said, adding that operators would be charged a fee of $5 million per year of operation.
The tender requires that by 2001 GSM should cover some 65 percent of Romania, most of the country's inhabited area, ministry sources said.

The ex-communist state is the last in the region to set up a digital GSM system. It currently operates an analogue technology mobile phone network covering eight cities, in partnership with Telefonica de Espana SA which has a 10-year licence.

The other four consortia which competed in the GSM tender included the U.S. telecoms group Motorola and Tele Danmark of Denmark, Italy's telecoms group Stet Spa and a joint venture between Telefonica de Espana and Romania's state telecoms network. -- Adrian Dascalu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
